headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error paths exist because Notion AI shares workspace state and external model backends while Dagster can surface workspace content, though direct pairwise integration is undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster is non-runnable and has no clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or network surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Notion AI output. Notion AI does read and summarize workspace pages, but the pair lacks a documented automatic bridge; any injection would require manual copy-paste or an external workflow, making the pathway unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Notion AI text into a Dagster config, ticket, or prompt field, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
IF an external integration is added that feeds Notion page text into Dagster automation, THEN the pathway becomes automatic.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste from Notion AI into operational prompts.
Add a review step for any text imported from Notion into Dagster workflows.
Use a fixed template for Dagster inputs that strips instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported text.
requires-engineering: isolate any future Notion-to-Dagster connector behind allowlisted fields.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends queries to vendor backends; Dagster is open-source and non-runnable here, so it is not a direct exfiltrator. The shared-risk path is workspace content being summarized in Notion and then reused elsewhere, which can leak sensitive material across work products even without host execution.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are available to Notion AI, THEN those contents can be exposed in generated summaries.
IF Notion AI output is copied into Dagster-managed docs or tickets, THEN sensitive content propagates to additional work products.
mitigations: Restrict Notion AI access to non-sensitive pages.
Mark sensitive pages as off-limits for AI use.
Review generated summaries before sharing them outside Notion.
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on exported AI summaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted with limited Notion-controlled actions. Because both lack overlapping unrestricted write surfaces, direct capability conflict is unlikely; the main overlap is shared workspace content, not concurrent mutation of the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF a future integration gives Dagster write access to the same Notion workspace objects, THEN write conflicts become possible.
IF multiple Notion AI instances edit the same page concurrently, THEN last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Avoid granting Dagster write access to Notion pages.
Use page-level ownership for shared docs.
Review concurrent edits before publishing.
requires-engineering: add locking or version checks for shared pages.
requires-engineering: route writes through a single orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative by downstream users. Dagster can then operationalize those outputs in pipelines or documentation, creating a plausible cascade from a mistaken summary to broader workflow errors, even though the exact pairwise handoff is undocumented.
conditions: IF a user copies Notion AI summaries into Dagster pipeline specs or runbooks without verification, THEN errors can cascade.
IF Dagster-generated artifacts are later treated as source-of-truth, THEN an initial Notion AI mistake can propagate.
mitigations: Require human verification of Notion AI outputs before reuse.
Label AI-generated text in downstream docs.
Keep Dagster specs separate from narrative summaries.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before pipeline changes.
requires-engineering: track source provenance for copied content.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and uses downstream model providers, while Dagster is open-source and non-runnable here; the pair can therefore move workspace content into a third-party AI service. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, but the retention and processing model differs enough to create a compliance gap for regulated workspace data.
conditions: IF regulated or restricted workspace content is processed by Notion AI, THEN third-party processing obligations apply.
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter retention rules than Notion's AI processing, THEN a policy mismatch exists.
mitigations: Exclude regulated content from Notion AI use.
Review vendor terms for retention and subprocessors.
Document approved data classes for AI use.
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level policy enforcement.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the AI workflow.
